description.value: The study investigated whether prolonged recreational amphetamine-type stimulant use is associated with gray matter volume reductions, comparing experienced ATS users, low exposure users and drug-naive controls using voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: The aim of the present study was to investigate if prolonged recreational ATS use leads to measurable alterations in brain morphology possibly indicating neurotoxic effects.

value: It is hypothesized that the incidental use of low doses ATS does not lead to lasting neurotoxic sequelae, whereas the regular and massive consumption is assumed to last in neurotoxic effects, indicated by gray matter volume reduction

description.value: The study compared three observational participant groups: experienced ATS users, low exposure users and drug-naive controls.

spans.text: Therefore, we studied gray and white matter densities in experienced ATS users, low exposure users with very limited ATS experience and drug-naive controls.
The study was carried out in accordance with the declaration of Helsinki from 1975 and was approved by the local ethics committee.

value: Experienced users showed several regions of lower gray matter volume in medial frontal regions, in particular the medial orbitofrontal cortex and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, compared to low exposure users. These differences might reflect effects of repeated ATS exposure, although pre-existing or confounding factors might also account for the between-group differences.

spans.text: However, compared to low exposure users, experienced users showed several regions of lower gray matter volume in medial frontal regions. In particular, differences in gray matter were found in the medial orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) and the medial dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (DACC) after correction for age, education, and time since last use of ATS.
